title: Tea Tourism in India: Darjeeling, Assam, Munnar, the Nilgiris and Beyond
seoTitle: Tea Tourism in India: Estates, Tastings and Stays | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Tea tourism in India: estate walks, factory visits, tastings and bungalow stays in Darjeeling, Assam, the Nilgiris, Munnar, Kangra, Sikkim and Valparai.
description: A guide to tea tourism in India: Darjeeling's hill estates and flushes, Assam's plains gardens around Jorhat and Dibrugarh, the Nilgiris around Coonoor and Kotagiri, Munnar's estates and tea museum, Kangra tea near Palampur, Sikkim's Temi garden, and Valparai, with estate walks, factory visits, tastings, bungalow stays and the best seasons.
dek: India grows some of the world's best-known teas, and many of the estates welcome visitors for walks, tastings and stays.

hero.alt: A tea garden on the hills of Darjeeling

intro: Tea shapes the landscape of several Indian hill regions: the steep gardens of Darjeeling, the clipped green slopes of Munnar and the Nilgiris, and, on the plains of the Brahmaputra, the vast estates of Assam. Many estates offer walks through the bushes, factory visits during the processing season, tastings and, in some cases, stays in old planters' bungalows.
Tea tourism is as much about people as landscape; the pluckers and factory workers whose work you see deserve respect and privacy.
quickAnswer: The main places for tea tourism in India are Darjeeling in West Bengal, the Assam gardens around Jorhat and Dibrugarh, the Nilgiris around Coonoor and Kotagiri, Munnar in Kerala, the Kangra valley around Palampur, Temi in Sikkim and Valparai in Tamil Nadu. Visitors can walk the estates, see factories in the plucking season, join tastings and stay in heritage bungalows. Spring and autumn are the best seasons in Darjeeling.
takeaways: Darjeeling tea has a Geographical Indication; its first flush (spring) and second flush (early summer) are prized.
Assam's tea grows on the plains, not in the hills; stay on a garden near Jorhat or Dibrugarh.
Munnar's tea museum explains the process from leaf to cup.
Factory visits depend on the plucking and processing season; check before you go.
Ask before photographing workers, and follow estate rules.

sections.heading: What you can do
list: Walk through the gardens with an estate guide.
Visit a factory to see withering, rolling, oxidation and drying (in season).
Join a tasting to compare flushes and grades.
Buy directly from estate shops or government-approved outlets.

sections.heading: A little history
paras: Commercial tea planting in India began in Assam in the 1830s, after the native Assam tea plant was identified, and spread to Darjeeling from the 1850s, using Chinese plants suited to the cooler hills. The Nilgiris and Munnar followed later in the 19th century. The estates were built on the labour of workers, many brought from other regions, whose descendants still work in the gardens today.

sections.heading: When to go
list: Darjeeling: March to May for first and second flush, and October to November for the autumnal flush and clear views.
Assam: October to April, avoiding the heavy monsoon.
Nilgiris and Munnar: most of the year; the monsoon is wet but green.

sections.heading: Buying tea
paras: Buy from estate shops, government-approved outlets or established tea merchants rather than roadside stalls selling unmarked 'Darjeeling' tea. Look for the Darjeeling logo and GI mark on packs, check the harvest and flush on the label, and store loose-leaf tea in an airtight container away from light.

safety: Follow estate rules and stay on paths.
Permits, e-passes and pass openings change; check official portals before you travel.
packing: A reusable bag for tea purchases

faqs.q: Where can I visit a tea estate in India?
faqs.a: Darjeeling, Assam, the Nilgiris, Munnar, Kangra, Temi in Sikkim and Valparai all have estates open to visitors.

faqs.q: What is first flush Darjeeling tea?
faqs.a: The spring harvest, usually from about March to April, known for its light, fresh character.

faqs.q: Can I stay on a tea estate?
faqs.a: Yes, several estates in Darjeeling, Assam, Munnar and the Nilgiris have bungalow stays.

faqs.q: Is Assam tea grown in the hills?
faqs.a: No, most Assam tea grows on the plains of the Brahmaputra valley.

faqs.q: When can I see tea being processed?
faqs.a: During the plucking season, which varies by region; check with the estate before visiting.

faqs.q: Which tea region is best for a first visit?
faqs.a: Darjeeling, for the combination of estates, the toy train and mountain views; Munnar is the easiest in the south.
